question: Mr. X starts from Point L and drives 5 km towards the east. He then takes a right turn, drives 6 km, turns right and drives 9 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 2 km, turns left, drives 4 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point O. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point L again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution:
Given:

Mr. X starts from Point L and drives 5 km towards the east.

He then takes a right turn, drives 6 km, turns right and drives 9 km.

He then takes a right turn and drives 2 km, turns left, drives 4 km.

He takes a final right turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point O.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2bd7442e9fc15049d5cf19e9c71a3c0a217ffe242d4e7ae7a8ad2a53da4b22ce.png] 

Thus, Mr. X should drive 8 km (9 km + 4 km - 5 km) in the east direction in order to reach Point L again.​

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.
